title: B2 · L21 — Phrasal verbs: emotions
topic: Phrasal verbs about emotions and reactions
description: Phrasal verbs para hablar de emociones: cheer up, calm down, freak out, break down, snap at.

questions.prompt: Un amigo está triste y quieres animarle.
questions.question: What does 'to cheer up' mean?
options: To become happier or make someone happier.
questions.explanation: 'Cheer up' significa animar(se). Puede ser intransitivo (dicho a alguien: 'Cheer up!') o transitivo con separación ('cheer someone up' / 'cheer up your friend'). Es uno de los phrasal más útiles y frecuentes para consuelo cotidiano. Nota: si el objeto es pronombre, va ENTRE el verbo y la partícula ('cheer him up', no 'cheer up him').
examples: Cheer up! It's really not the end of the world — you'll bounce back. → consuelo entre amigos
I brought her flowers and a bottle of wine to cheer her up after the break-up.

questions.prompt: Tu compañero está exagerando ante un problema menor.
questions.question: Complete: 'Please ___ ___. Nothing serious happened.'
questions.explanation: 'Calm down' significa tranquilizarse — se usa para pedir a alguien que modere una emoción intensa. Cuidado: decirle 'calm down' a una persona alterada puede sonar condescendiente en ciertos contextos, sobre todo si la persona tiene razón. En crisis reales, mejor 'take a breath' o 'take your time'.
examples: Take a deep breath and try to calm down before we discuss this properly. → gestión de conflicto
It took me hours to calm down after that awful phone call with my landlord.

questions.statement: 'To freak out' significa alterarse extremadamente por miedo, pánico o incluso emoción positiva.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Freak out' expresa una reacción emocional intensa: pánico, susto, ansiedad o alegría desbordada. Muy informal — no lo uses en registro corporativo o académico. En hablado joven, se oye constantemente: 'don't freak out', 'I'm freaking out', 'that freaked me out'.
examples: She completely freaked out when she saw the massive spider in the bathtub. → anécdota doméstica
Don't freak out — it's just a mock exam, nobody will see the results.

questions.text: She broke down in tears when she heard the news about her grandfather.
questions.explanation: 'Break down in tears' es colocación fija (romper a llorar, colapsar emocionalmente). Prosodia: pausa emocional tras 'tears', tono más contenido en 'grandfather'. Connected speech: 'broke down' se enlaza fluido; 'in tears' recibe énfasis emocional. Es fórmula típica de narración de duelo o momento traumático.
examples: He broke down completely at the funeral — he'd been holding it in all week.
She broke down in the middle of the presentation. It was heartbreaking to watch.

questions.prompt: Un colega te habla mal por estrés y luego se disculpa.
questions.question: What does 'to snap at someone' mean?
options: To speak angrily and impatiently to someone.
questions.explanation: 'Snap at' significa contestar mal, hablar bruscamente por irritación o estrés. Común al describir tensiones cotidianas y disculpas posteriores. La disculpa clásica: 'sorry I snapped at you, I'm just stressed'. Nota que el objeto siempre va tras 'at': 'snap AT someone', no 'snap someone'.
examples: Sorry I snapped at you earlier — I'm having a really rough week. → disculpa laboral honesta
He snapped at his assistant for no reason. Everyone in the office noticed.

questions.statement: 'To open up' puede significar 'volverse dispuesto a compartir sentimientos'.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Open up' emocionalmente significa abrirse, contar sentimientos íntimos. Muy común en contextos de amistad, pareja, terapia o salud mental. Es lo opuesto directo de 'bottle up' (reprimir). Nativos lo usan mucho en podcasts de bienestar, terapia y self-help.
examples: It took him years to finally open up about his childhood trauma. → conversación profunda
She finally opened up about her fears — first time in the ten years I've known her.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada phrasal verb emocional con su continuación natural:

pairs.right: It's not the end of the world.

questions.explanation: Todos son phrasal verbs de emociones intensas: cheer up (animar), calm down (tranquilizar), freak out (alterarse por pánico o sorpresa), break down (colapsar emocionalmente), lash out (reaccionar con agresividad verbal o física). Dominar este grupo permite narrar mini-dramas con precisión emocional.
examples: She lashed out at anyone who came near her — clearly having a terrible day. → conflicto laboral
He calmed down significantly after taking a long walk around the neighbourhood.

questions.prompt: Un amigo ha perdido a su mascota y le cuesta seguir adelante.
questions.question: Complete: 'I can't ___ ___ the loss of my dog. It's been really hard.'
questions.explanation: 'Get over' significa superar (una pérdida, decepción, ruptura, susto, enfermedad). Es uno de los phrasal más importantes sobre recuperación emocional en B2. También se usa en positivo: 'I can't get over how kind he was' (no puedo creerme lo amable que fue).
examples: It took her nearly a year to properly get over the break-up. → duelo emocional
I can't get over how kind he was to us that day. It really restored my faith in people.

questions.target: I need to calm down before the meeting. I don't want to lash out at anyone if things get heated.
questions.explanation: Combinación 'calm down' + 'lash out' en contexto profesional realista (reunión tensa, negociación difícil). Prosodia: tono reflexivo y auto-consciente, con énfasis en 'calm down' y 'lash out'. Nativos añaden 'honestly', 'genuinely' o 'you know how I get when I'm stressed' para reforzar la autoconciencia emocional.
examples: I'm really trying to calm down before I say something I'll seriously regret. → autoconciencia laboral
Just breathe and calm down — you've got this. You've handled way worse. → self-talk motivador

questions.prompt: Un artículo de salud mental habla de patrones tóxicos.
questions.question: What does 'to bottle up' emotions mean?
options: To suppress or hide them inside.
To share them with a friend.
questions.explanation: 'Bottle up' significa reprimir, guardar dentro (emociones negativas), como si las metieras en una botella con corcho. Se considera poco saludable psicológicamente y a menudo lleva a explotar más tarde. Es lo opuesto de 'open up'. Muy común en artículos de bienestar, terapia y self-help.
examples: Don't bottle up your feelings — talk to someone, even if it's just a friend.
He bottled up his anger for years, and eventually it came out in a huge way at work.

questions.statement: 'To perk up' significa volverse más enérgico o alegre.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Perk up' significa animarse, revivir, ponerse alegre — a menudo tras algo positivo o estimulante (café, buena noticia, ver a alguien). Es transitivo también: 'this coffee will perk you up'. Muy común en registro cotidiano; menos en escritura formal.
examples: She really perked up when she saw the puppy running towards her. → escena tierna
A strong coffee and a walk always perk me up in the morning. → rutina personal

questions.text: He completely freaked out when he realised he had lost his passport before the flight.
questions.explanation: 'Freak out' en contexto de pánico viajero — situación universalmente relatable. Prosodia: énfasis fuerte en 'completely freaked out' para transmitir la intensidad. Connected speech: 'when he realised' se enlaza suave 'wen-hi-rɪəlaɪzd'. 'Had lost' es past perfect, marca claramente la secuencia de eventos.
examples: I completely freaked out when I heard someone trying to open my hotel room door at 3 a.m.
Don't freak out — we can fix this. Let's just take it one step at a time. → apoyo en crisis

questions.prompt: Un amigo está pasando por un divorcio duro y no habla de nada.
questions.question: Complete: 'She really needs to ___ ___ about her divorce. Bottling everything up is making her ill.'
questions.explanation: 'Open up' (compartir sentimientos íntimos) es el antónimo directo de 'bottle up' (reprimir). El contexto explícito de salud mental confirma la elección. Es una recomendación muy típica en conversaciones sobre apoyo emocional entre amigos o familiares preocupados.
examples: It's really important to open up to someone you trust when things get tough. → consejo de salud mental
He finally opened up about his depression after months of silence. His family was relieved.

questions.target: I've been really down lately, but talking to my best friend always helps to cheer me up a bit.
questions.explanation: 'Be down' (estar deprimido, bajo de ánimo) + 'cheer someone up'. Prosodia: tono personal y reflexivo, casi confesional. Nativos añaden hedging emocional: 'you know', 'kind of', 'a bit' para no sonar demasiado dramáticos. Es fórmula típica de conversación cercana entre amigos.
examples: I've been feeling a bit down all week, honestly. Not sure what's up. → confesión honesta
A good film and a proper cup of tea always cheer me up when I'm having a rough day.

questions.prompt: Describes a alguien que atraviesa un duelo grave.
questions.question: What does 'to fall apart' mean emotionally?
options: To become extremely upset and lose emotional control.
questions.explanation: 'Fall apart' emocionalmente significa derrumbarse, perder el control emocional total. Se usa cuando alguien no puede lidiar con una situación devastadora. Es más intenso que 'break down' — implica desintegración prolongada, no sólo un momento de llanto. Muy usado en descripciones de duelo, crisis o burnout.
examples: She completely fell apart after her mother died. It took her years to rebuild.
He tried desperately to hold it together in public, but he was falling apart inside. → observación empática
